title: Devotion

image.credit: Gemeentemuseum Den Haag, The Hague; via arthistoryproject.com

altText: A portrait of a girl or young woman, painted in oil in an expressive, close-up way. The title suggests a quiet, inward mood.

source.verifiedBy: arthistoryproject.com artwork page text (title, year, medium, public-domain statement)

context: An oil painting on canvas by Piet Mondrian, dated 1908, in the Gemeentemuseum Den Haag. The source page tags it Portraits and Girls; Mondrian is better known for his later abstract paintings.

descriptions.k: This is a painting of a girl. The title is Devotion. That means caring about something very much. Look at her face. What do you think she might care about?
descriptions.g12: Piet Mondrian painted this girl in 1908. The title, Devotion, means loving or caring very much about something. Look at her face and the colors around her. What do you think she is feeling? What clues tell you?
descriptions.g35: Piet Mondrian painted Devotion in oil in 1908. The source page tags it Portraits and Girls. Mondrian later became famous for paintings made of straight black lines and blocks of color, but this is a much earlier work. Look at her face and the mood of the colors. What does the title lead you to expect?
descriptions.g68: Mondrian painted Devotion in 1908, long before the grids of black lines and primary colors that made him famous. This early oil portrait shows a girl, and its title points to an inward, emotional subject. How do color and expression suggest feeling, and what might connect this painting to the artist's later work?
descriptions.g910: Devotion (1908) is an early portrait by Piet Mondrian, better known for abstraction after about 1914. The title directs us toward inner feeling, while paint and color carry the mood. Looking at an early work like this can show how an artist develops. What visual choices here seem personal, and what might you compare with his later abstract work?
descriptions.g1112: Devotion (1908) is an early oil portrait by Mondrian, produced years before his rigorous abstraction. Seen with the later work in mind, it invites questions about continuity and rupture: does color already carry the expression? Be careful not to read the artist's later style backward onto this painting. What does the title ask of you, and what does the image resist?

k.analysis: Which did your eyes find first in Devotion, the girl's face or the colors near her, and what pulled you there?
k.line: Follow the curve of her head or shoulders with your finger. What shape does it make?
k.shape: Find a big shape in this painting. What does it remind you of?
k.color: Which colors do you see most in the painting? How do they make you feel?

k.meaning: The title is Devotion. What does that word make you imagine?
k.culture: Portraits have been painted for a long time in many places. Who would you paint a portrait of, and why?
k.technique: This painting is made with oil paint. What do you think the artist did with his brush?
k.personal: What quiet thing do you care about a lot, and how could you show it in a picture?
k.critical: What would you name this painting if you could pick a new title?

g12.culture: How could a portrait show what a person feels inside and not only how she looks?

g12.personal: How would you show the word devotion in a picture of your own?
g12.critical: What parts of the painting would you like to ask the artist about?

g35.daily: How do her face and the title Devotion work together to make you think of a feeling?
g35.emotion: What mood do you feel from this portrait, and what colors or shapes in it support your idea?

g35.color: Which colors does Mondrian use, and how do they work together to set the mood?
g35.texture: What can you tell from the brushwork about how the artist put on the paint?
g35.space: How does the artist place her within the picture so that she feels near or far?
g35.light: How do the bright and dark parts of the painting shape the way you see her face?

g35.technique: How would you describe the way this oil painting was made, based on what you see?

g68.daily: How do the girl's face and the title Devotion work together to suggest an inward mood?

g68.observation: Compare how the face is painted with how the surroundings are painted. What differences stand out?

g68.shape: How do the simplified shapes of the face and figure affect how real or symbolic she feels?
g68.color: How might the color choices be expressive rather than just descriptive?
g68.texture: What does the visible handling of the paint suggest about the painter's process?
g68.space: How does the space around the girl affect the feeling of intimacy in the portrait?
g68.light: How does the contrast of lighter and darker areas model the face and set the mood?
g68.meaning: The title names an emotion rather than a person. How does this change what a portrait can mean?
g68.culture: Mondrian later became known for abstract grids. What features in this early portrait might you compare with his later style, and what must you avoid assuming?
g68.technique: How might oil paint allow an artist to build mood through color and brushwork?
g68.personal: What do you imagine she is devoted to? Explain which details you used and what remains uncertain.

g910.daily: How does the title Devotion reframe what might otherwise read as a straightforward portrait of a girl?
g910.emotion: How does the painter use color and expression to build an emotional mood, and how does the title shape it?
g910.observation: Examine the transitions around the face and figure. What do they suggest about the painter's method?
g910.analysis: How does the composition create a hierarchy that places the girl's face at the center of attention?
g910.line: How do contours and the shapes of her form contribute to the portrait's quiet intensity?
g910.shape: How does the handling of form here simplify or emphasize the figure, and how does that affect her presence?
g910.color: How might color function symbolically in this portrait, and what are the limits of reading it that way?
g910.texture: What does the visible surface of the paint tell you about Mondrian's early working practice?
g910.space: How does the portrait's close, contained space affect the relationship between sitter and viewer?
g910.light: How does light model the face and contribute to the sense of an inner life?
g910.meaning: What does a title like Devotion invite viewers to project, and what visual evidence anchors or resists that?
g910.culture: How might a viewer who knows Mondrian's later abstraction look at this early portrait differently from one who does not?
g910.technique: How does this portrait show the expressive possibilities of oil paint before the painter moved toward abstraction?
g910.personal: What does this painting make you consider about how artists change over a career?
g910.critical: To what extent should we read an early work in light of an artist's later fame? Defend your answer.

g1112.daily: How does the painting balance the specificity of a portrait with the abstraction of its title, and which wins out?
g1112.emotion: How much of the portrait's emotional power comes from the sitter's expression, how much from the palette and how much from the viewer's expectations? Weigh the evidence.
g1112.observation: Scan the junctions between figure and ground. What do they imply about the painter's aims in 1908?
g1112.analysis: How does the composition direct attention while resisting a purely descriptive reading of the sitter?
g1112.line: How might the contours and masses of the figure anticipate or differ from the more radical simplification that came later?
g1112.shape: In what ways might the handling of form reflect the transitional period in which Mondrian was working?
g1112.color: How might the color relationships be read as expressive in a Symbolist sense, and what limits do we face in naming a movement not stated by the source page?
g1112.texture: How does the paint surface register process, and what does that reveal about expression versus control?
g1112.space: How does the portrait construct intimacy through space, and what does the painting withhold?
g1112.light: How does the painted light contribute to the sense of interior life, and which interpretations might differ?
g1112.meaning: How does a title naming an abstract quality complicate the notion of portrait as likeness?
g1112.culture: How should historians treat a work like this when it is seen mainly as a stage on the way to an artist's later fame?
g1112.technique: How does the use of oil here contrast with the strict means of Mondrian's later work, and what continuities can you argue for?
g1112.personal: How does your own experience of devotion or concentration color your reading of this painting?
g1112.critical: What would a persuasive argument look like that this portrait already contains the seeds of abstraction, and how would you counter it?

teacherNote.context: An early oil portrait by Piet Mondrian, dated 1908, in the Gemeentemuseum Den Haag. Mondrian is best known for his later abstract paintings; the source page tags this work Portraits and Girls.
directions: Have students draw a face that shows one feeling, then change only the colors to show a different feeling.
Discuss how an artist's style can change over a lifetime, comparing this early work with Mondrian's later grids if desired.
Ask students to propose alternative titles and explain how each changes the way we look.
